minutes.headline: Assessors voted to support a single tax rate and to lower the 41C senior exemption age from 70 to 65 for Town Meeting.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors held its March 4 meeting, covering the five-year revaluation public disclosure, a vote for a single tax rate, and signing of motor vehicle abatements and the excise commitment. They approved a personal property data collection RFP, a Chapter 61A partial release, the "How to read your Vision card" guide, and a request to move the board's web page. The main policy decision was recommending a lower eligibility age for the 41C exemption. The board then went into executive session under MGL chapter 59 section 60.

public_comment.topic: Applauded the transparency effort and the value of public eyes on the data; noted the long Zoom link read aloud does not work, only the short one.
Urged the board to ask the Vision representative to return for a public Q&A, with questions sent to him in advance.

budget_items.what_was_said: Commercial is a small share of the tax base, and the state discourages splitting the rate unless commercial is much larger, so the board historically uses a single rate.

budget_items.topic: Tax rate setting and bill calendar
budget_items.what_was_said: The state sets the tax rate after submissions; bills go out March 31st, with the payment and abatement date May 1st.
The first group of motor vehicle abatements was signed by two members, for vehicles sold or traded.
The first motor vehicle excise commitment for the year was signed.

budget_items.topic: Excess land value in Vision card guide
budget_items.what_was_said: The excess land value figure was set for the card guide, and condo base rate confirmed.
Current exemption is paid partly by state reimbursement and partly by the town; options to raise the amount and/or lower the age were costed per household.
Maximum gross income limits are not being changed.

budget_items.topic: Poverty data from the American Community Survey
budget_items.what_was_said: A member cited ACS 2022 poverty counts by age group as context for aid to residents.
One condo was taxed for land in error; other corrections were minor.

decisions.decision: Warrant article for the 41C age change to be pursued: the chair/member to contact the Select Board chair for the agenda and check wording with Town Counsel before the warrant deadline.
One member to draft a white paper on an ad hoc committee, usable as a template for the others, and report back on how long it will take.
Board agreed in principle to a policy and a shared assessor's office email directing public inquiries to the office, and to a log of inquiries.
Board will ask the Vision representative whether he can join a future public Q&A.
Reena to contact the Department of Revenue Division of Local Services about the exemption application timing language.
March 12 joint meeting with the Select Board for the classification hearing; next regular meeting March 18, then April 1, 15 and possibly 29.
At the March 25 community presentation, Reena will go first, with the representative and the 41C presenter following.
A member will contact the mapping vendor to turn off gradient colors and assign distinct colors per code.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted unanimously to recommend to Town Meeting that the 41C senior exemption eligibility age be lowered to 65, with no other changes.
The board voted unanimously to support a single tax rate for the next fiscal year, as it has historically done.
The board approved the request for proposals for a personal property data collection position and a partial release of Chapter 61A land at 372 Flat Hill Road.
The board supported the "How to read your Vision card" guide as amended, and voted to ask the web designer to move its page to the boards section of the town site.
The board moved into executive session by roll call at the end of the meeting.

why_it_matters: The 41C age change would widen who qualifies for a senior property tax exemption, and it is a warrant article residents will be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
The single tax rate vote means commercial and residential property are taxed at the same rate, which affects how the levy is divided on tax bills that go out March 31.
watch_next: March 12 joint meeting with the Select Board for the classification hearing, then the March 25 community presentation.
The 41C warrant article wording, to be checked with Town Counsel and put on the Select Board agenda before the warrant deadline.
